concerns: Proposal correctly identifies major dependencies (validated capture‑reagent buffer‑compatibility panels and ≥3 independent conditioned‑medium lots) — these must be completed prior to interpretation to avoid assay‑interference confounding.

Risk that observed loss of capture signal will be attributable to capture‑reagent incompatibility with excipients (assay interference) rather than true membrane/cargo loss; compatibility controls must be rigorous and include buffer‑only and detergent‑disrupted controls as proposed.

Translational uncertainty: even if an in‑vitro orthogonal signature is sensitive to downstream exposures, nonhuman‑primate/clinical biodistribution and clearance (per Driedonks 2022) may limit the utility of this gate for bridging to in‑vivo detectability or potency without additional in‑vivo recoverability checks, as the proposal notes.
conclusion: The proposal is plausible and appropriately conservative: cited canonical evidence provides indirect support for (A) sensitivity of EV analytical signals to handling and need for orthogonal characterization (MISEV2023), (B) source-cell/lot and translational considerations (Hermann 2023), and (C) large-animal biodistribution uncertainty that raises stakes for process gating (Driedonks 2022). However, none of the supplied canonical items directly demonstrate the specific causal link proposed (that defined freeze-thaw counts or particular nasal formulation-buffer classes reproducibly abolish the orthogonal intact‑EV signature while leaving bulk particle counts similar). That gap justifies the proposed experiment. Overall the design is supported by the canonical evidence but depends on execution of the stated assay-compatibility and replicate requirements before any interpretive or gating decisions.
evidence_gap: No canonical evidence demonstrates the specific experimental result claimed as the hypothesis outcome: i.e., reproducible abolition of an orthogonal intact‑EV (capture + particle co‑localization + protection) signature by defined downstream exposures (specific freeze‑thaw cycles or formulation-buffer classes) while bulk particle counts remain largely unchanged across independent conditioned‑medium lots. The proposal correctly frames this as a missing experiment.
